title: How to Kill Hidden PayPal Billing Authorizations
hook_text: Audit your PayPal recurring charges right now

beats.say: Old merchants can quietly pull money from your PayPal balance without ever asking your permission again.
beats.visual: A dark moody overhead shot of a sleek leather wallet resting beside an unbranded metal laptop on a dark walnut desk, lit by a single warm desk lamp.

beats.say: When you bought that one-off trial years ago, you likely granted permanent automatic billing authorization.
beats.visual: A silhouette of hands typing quietly on a matte black keyboard in a dimly lit minimalist office, shallow depth of field.

beats.say: Step one. Log into PayPal on a web browser, click the gear icon, and choose Account Settings.
beats.visual: Cinematic close-up of fingers hovering over an aluminum trackpad, soft glow reflecting off polished wood, camera at an extreme low angle.

beats.say: The phone app hides this menu, so a desktop browser or mobile web view works best.
beats.visual: A dark smartphone lying face down on a stone table next to a steaming ceramic coffee mug, morning shadows stretching across the surface.

beats.say: Step two. Click Money, Banks and Cards on the left, then scroll down to Automatic Payments.
beats.visual: A high-angle architectural still of an organized modern workspace with warm amber lighting and deep shadows, completely clutter-free.

beats.say: But here's the part nobody mentions. Every vendor you authorized over the years is still active.
beats.visual: A slow macro camera push toward a vintage brass padlock resting unlocked on top of a stack of dark paper notebooks.

beats.say: You'll likely spot at least one or two recurring charges you forgot about years ago.
beats.visual: A stark side profile of a person viewed from behind in a high-back chair, looking out a rainy floor-to-ceiling window at city lights.

beats.say: A $15/month subscription forgotten for 10 years drains $1,800 straight out of your pocket.
beats.visual: A neat stack of crisp hundred-dollar banknotes resting on a dark slate surface under a sharp single directional spotlight.

beats.say: Step three. Click on each outdated vendor name, select Cancel, and confirm Automatic Billing Cancellation.
beats.visual: A close-up of a hand firmly closing the lid of a dark, elegant notebook, signifying a decisive end.

beats.say: That instantly revokes their digital token so they can't charge your backup bank account ever again.
beats.visual: A heavy vintage iron vault door slightly ajar in a dimly lit corridor, moody cinematic documentary lighting.

beats.say: Take 5 minutes to audit this list twice a year to protect your hard-earned cash.
beats.visual: A luxury minimalist analog wristwatch resting on a dark granite nightstand, ticking second hand frozen in soft illumination.

beats.say: Follow for the money rules school never taught you, and stop silent cash drains today.
beats.visual: A calm, wide shot of an anonymous figure in an overcoat walking down a quiet architectural hallway toward a warm light.

caption: Old merchant permissions drain cash in the background without you noticing. Revoke them in under 5 minutes.
description: PayPal stores recurring merchant billing agreements indefinitely unless you manually revoke them. Learn the exact 3-step path in your browser settings to cancel active merchant permissions and plug silent money leaks.
first_comment: How many active automatic payments did you find sitting in your account?

facts.basis: Money Fact Sheet calculation: $15 * 12 months * 10 years = $1,800.
